priorStories.headline: Abyei market strike toll exceeds 220
priorStories.body:
Local authorities said more than 220 people were killed in Monday’s drone strike on Amiet Market, raising an earlier count of 153 as recovery work continued.

The strike ignited fuel stores in the market. Abyei officials blamed Sudan’s military, which had not publicly responded to the accusation, leaving responsibility unconfirmed.

priorStories.headline: Nigeria confirms imported Ebola case
priorStories.body:
Nigeria confirmed that a woman who recently arrived in Abuja from Uganda had Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus. She received care at a private hospital before laboratory testing confirmed the infection.

Authorities isolated the patient and began tracing contacts and monitoring health workers. No secondary infections were reported in the supplied information.

sources.name: Nigeria Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
World Health Organization Regional Office for Africa

priorStories.headline: Alberta rejects path toward separation from Canada
priorStories.body:
Alberta voters decisively rejected starting the legal process that could have led to a binding referendum on leaving Canada.

With more than 1.8 million votes counted and 81% of voting locations reporting, unofficial results showed about 75% favored remaining in Canada and 25% supported beginning the separation process.

priorStories.headline: UK expands air defense support for Saudi Arabia
priorStories.body:
The United Kingdom is adding RAF Typhoon patrols over Saudi territory after escalating Houthi attacks. An A400M transport aircraft and British military advisers will also be deployed.

The British government described the patrols as defensive counter-air missions and said its fighters would not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthis.

priorStories.headline: NATO expands Black Sea surveillance
priorStories.body:
NATO said it would send more maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems, drones and intelligence personnel to the Black Sea following deadly attacks on merchant ships. Forensic teams will also help investigate the incidents.

The alliance did not attribute the recent attacks to any country.

candidates.summary: Russia released retired American teacher Stephen Hubbard, who had been sentenced in 2024 to nearly seven years on mercenary charges that he denied. President Vladimir Putin told U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff during Ukraine-war talks in St. Petersburg that Hubbard was at the airport awaiting his return to the United States. The U.S. government had designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained.
candidates.title: Russia releases detained American during Putin-Witkoff talks

candidates.summary: The UK Office for National Statistics said annual consumer-price inflation rose to 3.5% in September from 3.1% in August, the highest rate since October 2025 and above economists' median forecast of 3.4%. Transport costs, particularly motor fuels, made the largest upward contribution. Core CPI increased to 2.8% from 2.6%.
candidates.title: UK inflation rises to 3.5%

candidates.summary: The UK Office for National Statistics provisionally estimated public-sector net debt at £3.005 trillion at the end of September, exceeding £3 trillion for the first time. Debt equaled 94% of gross domestic product, 0.7 percentage points lower than a year earlier. September borrowing was £24.5 billion, £1.8 billion more than a year earlier and £1.9 billion above the official forecast.
candidates.title: UK public debt provisionally exceeds £3 trillion

candidates.summary: Doctors amputated Australian federal lawmaker Helen Haines' right leg after abandoning efforts to save it, her husband said; her left leg had been amputated Monday. Haines remained in critical but stable condition after being repeatedly struck by a vehicle in Wangaratta. A man charged over the incident appeared in court Wednesday, did not seek bail or enter a plea, and remained in custody. Police had not established a motive.
candidates.title: Australian lawmaker loses both legs after vehicle attack
